answer: A Sybil defence is stake-bonded admission with slashing: an agent joins by locking a deposit peers burn if it is caught running duplicate identities, and the ledger ties that bond to one attested enclave. A thousand puppets cost a thousand deposits, so the price of n identities scales linearly while the payoff from one vote stays flat. Reputation reinforces this: each identity is pinned to a persistent key, so a copy reborn under a fresh jade mask inherits nothing. Honest agents gather a nebula of attestations, an opal no clone can counterfeit, so attackers buy identities nobody trusts.
